qc/runs/coldwater-strict-2026-10-02-r16/raw-evidence-index.json (all 22 artifact hashes recomputed and matched; scripted results editor/runtime/polish/restart JSON read)
evidence: No credible defect in this row's scope; six lesser points recorded. REACHABILITY: instruction.md says 'read the six notes in /instructions' and exactly six are copied by environment/Dockerfile:14 (overview, ui, behaviour, security, integration, policy). integration.md:3-11 states every launch fact that tests/test.sh:97-111 relies on: node server.js from a cwd outside /app, 'Resolve files from their actual location', port 3000 with 'PORT is set to 3000 at launch', GET /api/health, Express and better-sqlite3 'through NODE_PATH' (environment/Dockerfile:3,9-12 and tests/Dockerfile install the same pinned versions), DB_PATH 'including when the app runs from a writable copy outside /app' (test.sh:98-102), and the symlink rule (test.sh:72-83). task.toml:22 network_mode = public, so a formatter/parser can be fetched and vendored; integration.md:5 says 'Include everything needed at runtime; opening the finished app must not require an install or build step'. The seed is empty and both instruction.md and integration.md:7 say so ('contains no user snippets or starter implementation'). The hardest capabilities are reachable with ordinary browser features: preview isolation and network refusal via a sandboxed iframe plus CSP connect-src 'none', dynamic-evaluation refusal via CSP without unsafe-eval, grapheme handling via Intl.Segmenter, time limit via loop guards. Measured support: the scripted golden on these exact bytes, installed with solve.sh and launched as test.sh launches it (uid 65534, env -i, DB_PATH, cwd outside /app) reports true for every one of the 3 gate, 43 Functional and 6 Polish criteria in results/editor.json, runtime.json, polish.json and a real restart in restart.json; all 22 hashes in the evidence index match (hosted-run files on LF-normalised bytes). That is scripted evidence in the agent image, not a configured judge run and not a target-model build; no judge run exists for these bytes. AMBIGUITY: I walked every functional, polish and gate criterion against the notes looking for a second reasonable reading that the criteria would fail. Where the notes leave a choice the criteria accept both readings (single-caret undo granularity ui.md:9 vs cw_undo_restores_caret; triple click 'with or without its line break'; indent width 'the same indent'; quote style after Format; console cleared or kept between runs in cw_basic_run_output; old-revision restore 'either refused or added on top'; first Find match may already be current; 'about five seconds' graded at ten). NOTES (none is graded against a conforming reading): (1) behaviour.md:3 'The browser may execute supported code in the preview' never says what is unsupported; a builder who enforces security.md:5 with a nonce-only CSP would silently disable inline handler attributes, which cw_html_preview requires ('a button whose inline handler changes visible text'). I judge this not a second reasonable reading because security.md:5 gives a closed list (eval, Function, WebAssembly, new workers, dynamic module imports) and behaviour.md:3 says 'A complete .html file replaces that document', but the wording is loose. (2) behaviour.md:3 asks for 'a one-based line number for a thrown error ... and a Promise rejection that nothing handles; the message is the text of the Error or rejected value'. For a rejection whose value is not an Error (Promise.reject('text')) the browser's unhandledrejection event carries no line, so read literally that part is not obtainable without source instrumentation; cw_promise_rejection_message_and_line only uses new Error, so nothing unreachable is graded. (3) behaviour.md:5 'pending timer or Promise callbacks until that run settles' does not define settling for requestAnimationFrame loops or event listeners, and implies any endless animation is always a time-limit failure; criteria use only timers and source loops. (4) ui.md:5 'current line and column, both counted from one' does not say whether an emoji or a decomposed letter counts as one column; cw_caret_navigation_and_line_numbers lets the judge choose the fixture and does not exclude such characters, though its three-short-lines shape makes an ASCII fixture the natural one. (5) behaviour.md:11 'If the snippet I have open gained a newer revision elsewhere, say so and keep my draft' does not say what happens when the open copy has no unsaved change; only the dirty case is graded. (6) An endless synchronous loop cannot be ended from the parent of a same-process sandboxed iframe, so the five-second budget in behaviour.md:5 in practice needs loop instrumentation or process isolation; the notes give no hint, which is difficulty rather than unreachability (the golden does it and passes cw_time_limit_recovery in results/runtime.json).
suggested_fix: Optional wording tightening only: in behaviour.md:3 replace 'supported code' with a plain statement that ordinary inline scripts and handler attributes of a complete HTML file run, and limit the line-number promise for unhandled rejections to rejections that carry an Error; in ui.md:5 say that a visible character counts as one column.
